extracted.intended_audience: authors, copyeditors, proofreaders, indexers, and publishers (people preparing or producing manuscripts and published works)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for preparing, editing, proofreading, and publishing book and journal manuscripts, including punctuation, citations, permissions, proofs, and production practices. Covers house-style decisions used by editors, indexers, and production staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parentheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage and treatment of parentheses in running text, indexes, citations, lists, captions, and table titles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See guidance on parallel structure, auxiliary verbs, correlative conjunctions, en dashes, lists and outlines, in prepositional phrases, subheads, paraphrasing, scholarly abbreviations, sentences in, marking proofs, font, back-to-back parentheses, and interactions with other punctuation (brackets, colons, commas, exclamation points, multiple sets, periods, question marks). Also notes on translations of quotations and telephone numbers, time zones, and glosses/translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parenthetical elements in sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: How to handle parenthetical elements within sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to rules at 6.48, 6.51, 6.85, 6.95; see also parentheses and punctuation entries for interactions and punctuation conventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participles and participial phrases
rubrics_metrics.description: Formation, uses, and common problems with participles (past, present, fused, dangling) and participial phrases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers formation, dangling participles, participles as adjectives, adverbs modifying participles, be-verbs with participles, participles vs. gerunds, negation, and table-title uses. Hyphenation of compound terms with participles is referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particles (in verbs and names)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of particles in phrasal verbs and personal names and their alphabetizing and capitalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes negating particles, placement in phrasal verbs (5.102), and alphabetizing/personal-name rules (16.71,16.84; capitalization 8.4-8.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts and parttitles (book divisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for parts of books: part titles, division into parts, pagination, numbering, and manuscript-preparation concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes format of terms, introductions to parts, editing and submission guidelines, table of contents entries, and index treatment for parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts of speech (reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification and reference of parts of speech (adjectives, adverbs, articles, conjunctions, interjections, nouns, prepositions, pronouns, verbs) as they affect style decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See individual sections for rules tied to usage and capitalization as relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Passive voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition and guidance for use and avoidance of passive constructions and interaction with participles and tense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References include definitions, relationship to dangling participles, infinitives in passive constructions, linking verbs, long-passive constructions (with by), and use with past participles.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF files (production and submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards and best practices for using PDF files in manuscript submission, proofs, digital artwork, continuous publishing, navigation, searching, annotations, timestamps, and testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers using PDFs for edited manuscripts, digital artwork, prepress proofs, as content proof, functional features, hyperlinks, front matter, editorial and proofreading workflows, indexer use, searching and testing, line break issues, time/user stamps, and use in continuous publishing models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review (mention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgement of peer review as part of the publication/editorial process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry references peer review at 2.5; context implies its role in manuscript preparation and production workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissions (rights and process)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and procedures for obtaining permissions for previously published or third-party material and special types of material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers definition and criteria, obtaining permissions (archives' restrictions; for an author’s own work), fees and record keeping, blanket permissions, permissions in illustration credit lines, role of counsel, sample letters, automating the process, interview/photo releases, orphan works, permissions for multiauthor volumes, manuscript and editorial concerns, permissions for particular items (illustrations, poetry, tables, unpublished works), checking and granting permissions, and where to note permissions (copyright page, acknowledgments). Includes cautions about complexity and when permissions are unnecessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible changes to quoted and referenced materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules and cautions about what editorial or author changes are permissible in quoted/referenced material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic approach (2.44), overview (13.7–8), punctuation and capitalization cautions, spaces and spacing, initial articles (a/an/the), non-English materials, typography and layout, titles of works, and interaction with translations and editorial interpolations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent URLs (permalinks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and citation of persistent URLs or permalinks in source citations and online references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References at 14.9, 14.15 for inclusion and formatting of permalinks in citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal communications (citations)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to cite personal communications in author–date and notes-bibliography reference systems, and permissions for such communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author-date system: general guidance (15.53). Notes and bibliography system: general guidance (14.214). Permissions references: 2.2, 2.3. Includes handling of posts on private forums and social media messages as personal communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs and illustrations (credits and permissions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on original/commissioned photographs: permissions, credit lines, halftones, reproduction quality, releases, previously published images, and source citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes commissioned vs. original, copyright registration forms, fair use, halftones and figures, labeling in illustrations, permissions and credits in captions and credit lines, reproduction quality, releases for photographs, handling of previously published images, and distinguishing illustration credits location and format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: Identification and treatment of plagiarism as a publishing and copyright concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries reference plagiarism issues to copyright and permissions sections (1.91, 4.75, 4.92).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain-text files
rubrics_metrics.description: Use and characteristics of plain-text files in production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referenced as a file type (p. 985) with implicit considerations for electronic workflow and cleanup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phrases (types and usage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of adjectival, adverbial, participial, parenthetical, restrictive/nonrestrictive, and other phrase types and their effect on meaning and punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers articles affecting meaning, introductory phrases, parallel structure, placement, use with not/only...but also, with such as/including, with the more/the less, use as words, verb phrases, and interaction with clauses and parenthetical elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical quantities and units
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for expressing physical quantities, dimensions, simple fractions, whole numbers plus fractions, abbreviations and symbols, and interaction with scientific notation and SI units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes use with abbreviations and symbols, dimensions examples, simple fractions, and references to International System of Units and metric-system guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurals (formation and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on forming plurals of nouns, abbreviations, foreign words, titles, units, collective nouns, and special cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers apostrophes, alternative forms, anomalies, conventional pluralization of abbreviations and initialisms, plurals used as words, plurals of proper names, plural nouns that are singular in sense, and special numeric/plural issues for units and centuries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods (punctuation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for periods with abbreviations, inside/outside sentence endings, academic and professional designations, biblical citations, business abbreviations, and in legal-style citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes guidance on omission in some technical abbreviations, use with eras, time designations, units of measurement, and spaces after periods (single space guidance referenced elsewhere). Also cross-references ellipses and other punctuation interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permalinks/persistent URLs and online identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of DOIs, URLs, permalinks, and other persistent identifiers in text, citations, and metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to punctuation and typography considerations for URLs/DOIs in text, and inclusion in citation systems (14.x, 15.x).

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent and percent sign
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage rules for percent/percentage and the percent sign across contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References given at 3.82, 7.89 (sec.1), 9.18 for context-sensitive use; see also numerals and formatting sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreader’s marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard proofreader’s marks and conventions for marking manuscripts and proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes capitalization changes, circling comments and instructions, deletions, em spaces, examples (figures), extensive changes, font changes, items to be spelled out, legibility, paragraph and indentation changes, placement of marks, position/alignment changes, punctuation changes, spacing changes, stet, transposition marks, and list of marks (fig. 2.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofreading (process and standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards, procedures, and responsibilities for proofreading at different stages of production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines proofreading, assigns responsibility for errors, double-checking, editorial style sheet use, example workflows, global changes and extensive changes, interaction with indexing, metadata, stages of proofs, independent professionals, checks for fonts/illustrations/tables/page numbers/quotations/running heads/sense/spelling, schedule and stages, revised proofs, and standards for electronic publications and PDF workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs (stages and handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of proofs, types (digital, galley), stages of proofing, marking, and indexing from proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers digital proofs, indexing from proofs, marking proofs for indexing, production checklist placement, stages (first pages/galley proofs, revised proofs), press and prepress interactions, and handling of cover and jacket proofs and F&Gs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepositional phrases and prepositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on formation, placement, function, avoidance of overuse, ending sentences with prepositions, idiomatic uses, and parallel structure related to prepositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines prepositional phrases, discusses placement, limiting vs. nonlimiting, objective case, interaction with pronouns and nominalizations, participation in phrasal verbs, and specialized guidance for headline-style capitalization and non-English languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefixes and hyphenation
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for prefixes, combining forms, hyphenation with prefixes, division of words, and exceptions for particular languages and numerical expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes combining forms, division with prefixes, treatment in Greek/Hebrew/Russian, SI units usage, use of mid-/pre-/post-/proto-/pseudo-/pro-/retro-, and guidance on standing-alone prefixes and hyphenation conventions (7.82, 7.89 etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprints and electronic-first publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of preprints and electronic publications published before print, and their role in continuous-publishing models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to preprints as defined and their handling in citation and publishing workflows (1.113, 14.173), and PDF use for continuous publishing (1.82, 14.174).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pronouns (agreement and bias-free language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive guidance on pronoun classes, antecedents, agreement (number and person), case, gender, misuse, singular they and gender-neutral language, reflexive/intensive forms, and language-specific issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers antecedents (absent/identified), personal pronouns after linking verbs, possessive pronouns, pronouns in contractions, induction of bias-free language, singular they usage and its cross-references (5.48, 5.252, 5.256), pronouns in non-English languages, and special uses and classes (demonstrative, indefinite, interrogative, reciprocal, relative).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possessives (formation and exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for forming possessives including basic rules, compound terms, joint and separate possession, possessives with gerunds, pronoun possessive forms, punctuation, and possessives of names ending in s.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers apostrophes in possessives, possessives vs. contractions, possessives in phrases with appositives, genitive forms, possessives in titles and indexes, possessives with italicized or quoted terms, possessives of plural nouns, and joint vs. separate ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods of time and cultural periods
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for naming and formatting periods of time (centuries, decades, eras, geological/cultural periods).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes numeric and descriptive designations, prehistoric cultural periods, traditional names, and cross-references to dates and time-designation guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plates and illustrations lists (numbering and indexing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for defining plates, numbering, indexing, lists of plates, text references, and when to include or omit plate items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines plates, indexing conventions, lists placement (e.g., fig.1.7), numbering rules, and text references; cross-references galleries and illustration credit lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication details and citation elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Required components and formatting of publication details (place, date, publisher, edition, form) for source citations in notes-bibliography and author-date systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes basic formats (14.127, 15.6, 15.9, 15.14, 15.25), handling of absent details, special guidance for works before 1900, dissertations/theses, journals, no-date treatments, and metadata considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing agreements (rights and obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Key provisions and editorial implications of publishing agreements between authors and publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes basic provisions, author’s warranties, limitations on alterations, copyright tasks assigned to publisher, subsidiary rights, open-access and non-English rights, examples (figs.), multiauthor-volume provisions, journal-article agreements, and special clauses such as 'no derivatives'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers and house style
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher responsibilities, house-style conventions, metadata, author communications, editorial processes, and publisher naming conventions in front matter and citations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers publisher addresses, agreements, archiving practices, copublications, distribution, logos, editorial house style for indexes/tables/citations, web presence and metadata, imprints and parent companies, and when/where to omit publisher names in citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishing schedule and production checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical production schedule components (manuscript editing, proofreading, indexing) and a basic publishing timetable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes production schedule examples and figures (fig. 2.1, 2.2), indexing schedule, manuscript editing and proofreading stages, proofing stages, and volume editor responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation (general functions and interactions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fundamental functions of punctuation, typographic considerations, interactions with italics and abbreviations, marking manuscripts and proofs, spacing conventions, and interactions with mathematical content and URLs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses basic function (6.1), punctuation in captions/tables/electronic files, punctuation errors, marking manuscripts/proofs, mathematical punctuation, multiple marks at same place, non-English materials, permissible changes in quoted material, spaces following punctuation, and punctuation of URLs/DOIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proofs and proofing for indexes
rubrics_metrics.description: Special guidance for indexing from proofs, marking proofs for indexing, and proofreading indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References indexing from proofs (16.4, 16.102, 16.105, 16.108, 16.117, 16.133) and marking proofs for indexing (16.117–21, fig.16.1) as part of production checklist.
